title: The whole system on one page
html:
Every finding on this site, boiled down to what you actually do on draft night. Every rule links to its write-up — click through to see the data and how sure we are.

Before you pick

  • Bring a list and follow it. Sticking to credible rankings beats drafting by feel by about ten points of season strength. Everything else on this page is a fight over the last one. Finding 03
  • Spend your prep on players, not draft tricks. Knowing who's good beats clever pick order about 40 to 1. Finding 24
  • Draft off ADP, and don't reach. In 9,000 simulated leagues, taking the market in order won titles two and a half times as often as a typical drafter — and beat every custom ranking we could build, including our own. Finding 32

Rounds 1–3: running backs

  • Open RB-RB-RB. In 1,440 simulated seasons of our league it won the title 20% of the time — two and a half times the fair share. Finding 01
  • The reason: RBs run out first. Running back value falls off almost twice as fast as receiver value, and the waiver wire never restocks it. Finding 23 · Finding 07
  • Don't get talked into Zero RB. In our standard-scoring league it won 9.7% of titles — barely better than autopilot. Finding 02

Rounds 4–8: quarterback and receivers

  • Take your first QB in rounds 4–6. Anywhere from 2 to 8 is fine; the real mistake is waiting past round 10 and planning to stream. Finding 14 · Finding 06
  • Target the top receiver on a bad team. A team's #1 receiver coming off a losing season hits top-24 43% of the time, against 25% for the rest of the mid rounds. The draft tool marks these with a green ◆. Finding 08
  • Buy targets, not efficiency. A receiver with lots of targets and modest points is a buy; big points on few targets don't repeat. Finding 17
  • Touchdown luck resets. Fade last year's TD-lucky players, buy the unlucky ones — the tool marks both. Finding 16
  • Skip the bounce-back-discount receiver. Top-20 two years ago, cratered last year, "value" price now: that profile busts 53% of the time. Finding 09
  • Ignore "injury-prone" at QB and WR. Missed time doesn't carry over at those positions — take the discount other drafters give you. Mild caution at TE only. Finding 18
  • Squint at 29–30-year-old receivers at mid-round prices. That age band busted most, though the sample is thin. Finding 10

Rounds 9–12: tight end and the bench

  • **Tight end: elite in rounds 1–4, or wait for round 10. Never the middle.** Early tight ends beat the receivers and backs taken at the same picks 69% of the time and bust at half the rate. But after round 4 the odds fall off a cliff, so rounds 5–9 pay a real pick for round-12 odds. Finding 33 · Finding 05
  • A second QB or TE is a free choice — the timing isn't. Take one late or not at all; never early. Finding 20
  • Don't draft to a roster template. Any shape you'd plausibly want is worth the same as just taking value — but only if you work the waiver wire. If you're a set-and-forget manager, stay balanced and take the backup QB. Finding 34
  • Don't overload the bench with lottery-ticket RBs. The stash-a-back theory buys about one percent of championships. Finding 19
  • Your stud RB's handcuff is insurance, not profit. Owning him pays out exactly when your starter sits and adds zero edge overall — take him if he's free, never reach. Finding 13

Rounds 13–15: kicker and defense

  • Spend your last two picks here, and don't think hard. Last year's kicker stats predict almost nothing. Finding 04
  • Defense: one number — the opponent's implied total. Draft whoever faces the worst offenses early, then stream all season. Finding 27
  • Kicker: pick the offense and the dome, not the leg. Finding 28
  • "He's on a better offense" is not a tiebreak. Vegas does know which offenses will score — it just doesn't help you pick between two skill players. Finding 30

During the season

  • The waiver wire is maintenance, not strategy. Worth 5–12 points a season, mostly patching QB and kicker — but a usage jump (targets, carries) is the one thing worth claiming early. Finding 22
  • Streaks mean nothing. A hot or cold last three weeks predicts zero about next season — price the full season. Finding 15
  • Read injury tags like this: Out and Doubtful mean zero. When a player is Questionable, he plays 69% of the time at about 83% strength. Finding 21
  • Don't overthink start/sit matchups. Opponent and weather are worth about a point a week at best, and Vegas already priced them. Finding 26

Why you can trust the averages

  • **A round-1 pick returns a weekly starter 81% of the time; round 15, 5%.** Early picks buy floors, late picks buy lottery tickets — spend them that way. Finding 29
  • **Losing two finals in a row is a coin-flip outcome, not a broken plan.** Finding 12 · Finding 11
